title: v2 stores: a log read never fails on a line still being written
head: 1b13630572360d082465e2f30e4b2680a09b9ea1
brief: _Store._append writes a JSONL line under the module _lock; _read_lines takes no lock, so a reader landing mid-line saw an unterminated last line and raised StoreError ('path:N: Unterminated string ...'). In the product a transcript route, chat_read or the runner's read_log could fail transiently. _read_lines now reads bytes and, only when the file does not end in a newline and the LAST line fails JSON parsing, treats it as a write in progress and returns the rows before it. A write cut mid multi-byte character (UnicodeDecodeError 'unexpected end of data' at EOF inside the last line) is treated the same way. Unchanged: a malformed interior line, a malformed newline-terminated last line (LF or CRLF), any other invalid UTF-8 and non-object JSON all still raise with the same path:N: messages; an unterminated last line that parses is still returned. New torn_read test covers these plus a concurrent writer/reader case.
focus: correctness, including under concurrency and across the ordering of events
handling of untrusted input, and safety-boundary changes
test coverage of the new behaviour: would the tests fail without the change?
claims in the description against the evidence in the diff and tests

ground_truth.mechanism: records are split with str.splitlines(), which also breaks at U+2028/U+2029/U+0085, VT, FF and FS/GS/RS; json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) leaves those raw inside a string, so one record reads back as unparseable fragments and the whole log (a chat's transcript, chat_read) becomes unreadable
ground_truth.evidence: stores.threads.log(thread.id, 'you', 'a\u2028b') then stores.threads.read_log(thread.id) raises StoreError on the interior fragment
ground_truth.source: lead review of #267 (transcript record, 2026-10-19); fixed in d440184 with a separator_characters test
